analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. It touches docs/provider/cli-reference.md (a benchmark schema 5 note and one new daemon-passthrough row for DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS at head line 1759) and docs/reference/configuration.md (new and updated rows at head lines 393-395). No executable code, trust-boundary logic, attestation, encryption or authorization paths change.

Security-relevant notes:
(1) The docs say the two scheduler geometry knobs are forwarded to the LaunchAgent. That adds two shell-controlled tunables to the daemon environment. They are performance and memory-geometry parameters that affect KV charges and activation peaks (A-004 and T-029 availability only). They do not touch the prefix-cache crypto, scope, TTL or gating in T-041, and the docs state that malformed values fall back to defaults. The doc claims about the passthrough list and Swift parsing and clamping behavior cannot be verified from the supplied evidence, because LaunchAgent.swift and EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift are not in the batch. The wider-chunk rows (a 2048 default for Gemma 4) may affect memory and DoS posture, but that is a code-behavior question, not a doc regression.
(2) The base docs mention the passthrough table lists 'remaining SSD-prefix and memory-cap tunables' as not forwarded. That is unchanged and consistent with the new rows.
(3) The head cli-reference passage on prefix-cache defaults and the SSD env variables is unchanged context. It is consistent with T-041 (single DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch, TTL only shortenable).

No threat-model update appears necessary for these docs. The code that implements the forwarded knobs should be reviewed in the PR's code batches, if any, for bounds checking of large chunk values (memory exhaustion).
